publish-boundary-test.ref: server/killSwitchSharing.test.ts (13) + server/publishChokePoint.test.ts (13). socialPublish.ts changed in two ways and both are covered. (1) The kill-switch check was EXTRACTED to killSwitchBlockedPlatforms so igAutopost — an autonomous cron measured at 116 live posts in prod — could share the operator's emergency stop instead of bypassing it. killSwitchSharing.test.ts pins the guard's decisions (global / publishing / per-platform, the DENY audit record naming WHICH switch fired, and the deliberate fail-open when switch state is unreadable) AND pins that the extraction left publishToSocial behaviourally identical — including the partial-block case where one platform is stopped and the other still publishes, which is the behaviour most likely to be lost in an extraction. (2) A `link` field was added, because its absence was WHY nickActions.socialPost reached around the door to metaSocial.socialPost; pinned through to postToFacebook. publishChokePoint.test.ts holds the claim gates at contentAdmin.publishCarousel and nickActions.socialPost, and adds a structural sweep asserting no NEW file can import the low-level publishers — the part that makes it stick, since adStudio was fixed alone on 2026-07-25 and this identical defect survived on three other surfaces. Both structural assertions red-green verified: planting a file that imports postToInstagram fails the sweep by name; removing igAutopost's guard branch while keeping the call fails its pin. CADENCE IS NOT CLAIMED — this change deliberately did NOT apply the feed cap to igAutopost, because policy v7 sets maxFeedPostsPerDay=2 while the autoposter has been doing 3/day on 8 of the last 14 active days, and that conflict is the operator's to resolve, not this PR's to decide silently. PR #1127.

cron-fail-closed.ref: server/ros083BriefPriorities.test.ts (9), mutation-verified three ways. The cron file changed here is cron/jobs/morningBrief.ts, and the fail-closed question has an unusual answer for it, so it is worth being precise rather than reciting the pattern.  THIS JOB HAS NO SEND-OR-HOLD DECISION TO GET WRONG. It reads, it composes text, and it calls sendTelegram exactly once at the end — one message, to the owner, with no customer contact anywhere on the path. There is no claim, no queue drain, no per-recipient loop, and nothing to double-send. The failure modes that fail-closed exists to prevent (duplicate customer SMS, a re-fired batch, a half-claimed row) cannot occur here.  WHAT COULD GO WRONG INSTEAD is the brief being WRONG rather than absent, and that is the direction this change moves. Nothing new can throw: buildDecisionsBlock is pure and total — every branch returns a string, there is no path through it that can reject — and it is called inside the SAME try/catch that already wrapped the topDecisions read. The catch still logs and still continues; what changed is that it now assigns an explicit UNAVAILABLE line instead of leaving "". So the job's success/failure surface to the scheduler is byte-for-byte what it was: sendMorningBrief still returns { recordsProcessed: 1, details } on the happy path, still returns { details: 'DB unavailable' } when the top-level db() handle is null, and still throws only from the reads that could already throw.  The one behavioural change on the failure path is that the brief now SAYS the priority queue could not be read. That is strictly more conservative than before: previously the LLM filled the mandated 'Top 3 priorities' section from whatever else was in the data blob and the operator received invented priorities formatted as queue-backed ones.  topDecisions gained `queryable: boolean`, which is additive. Checked rather than assumed: shared/bridgeShapes.ts TopDecisionsShape is a non-strict z.object, so the other consumer (routes/nour-os-query.ts, which hands the result to the Telegram bridge) keeps parsing unchanged, and server/__tests__/bridge-shapes.test.ts stays green — including its drift case, which asserts a fixture MISSING totalLive is rejected.  Mutations verified RED and each file restored byte-identical: letting the unqueryable case fall through turns 1 case red, returning "" on a genuinely empty queue turns 2 red, deleting the prompt rule turns 1 red. NOT CLAIMED: no live cron tick, no LLM call, no Telegram message — the scheduler-surface claims above are read from cron/scheduler.ts and cron/index.ts, not measured against a deployed run.

operator-walkthrough.ref: WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES, on a phone — the Nick AI morning brief in Telegram, every day around 7am. This is the last ROS-083 site and the only one that is not a rendered number, which changes both the failure and how you check it.  BEFORE: when the opportunity queue could not be read, the TOP DECISIONS block was left as an empty string. That does not read as "nothing to decide" to the model. The FORMAT RULES in the same prompt MANDATE a "Top 3 priorities" section, so with no block the LLM wrote the operator's priorities for the day FROM SCRATCH, out of whatever else happened to be in the data blob, and Telegram delivered them looking exactly like a queue-backed list. There is no visual tell — no zero, no empty state, no grey card. The brief simply reads like a normal brief and the priorities in it are invented. It is the one site in this class you can act on before you have finished reading it.  Three different states produced that identical silence: the queue was read and is genuinely clear · the queue could NOT be consulted (no database handle, or migration 0099 unapplied so revenue_opportunities does not exist — the service returned both as an ordinary empty result) · the read threw.  AFTER: the block is ALWAYS present and names which state produced it. A genuinely clear queue reads "TOP DECISIONS: none — the opportunity queue was read successfully and holds no actionable decisions right now (3 live, 2 excluded for no contact consent, 1 snoozed)", carrying the counts that prove it was actually read. An unconsultable queue reads "TOP DECISIONS: UNAVAILABLE ... This is NOT the same as an empty queue", and the prompt now tells the model what to do with that: lead the priorities section with "Priority queue unavailable this morning — these are not queue-backed" and present nothing as ranked or evidence-backed. The template fallback path (used when the LLM call itself fails) already interpolates the same block, so it inherits the honesty for free.  `topDecisions` gained `queryable: boolean` so the unconsultable case is distinguishable at the source rather than guessed at the call site. Additive and safe for the bridge: shared/bridgeShapes.ts TopDecisionsShape is a non-strict z.object, so the nour-os-query consumer keeps parsing unchanged.  The block-builder was EXTRACTED to `buildDecisionsBlock` for one honest reason, stated in the code: the surrounding function is ~400 lines of sequential reads and cannot be exercised in a unit test, which is exactly why this survived. The idiom is not new — the exceptions block twenty lines below already emits "waiting-customer count UNKNOWN (read failed — check the SMS admin)".  EVIDENCE: server/ros083BriefPriorities.test.ts (9), MUTATION-VERIFIED THREE WAYS — letting the unqueryable case fall through turns 1 red, returning "" on a genuinely empty queue turns 2 red, deleting the prompt rule turns 1 red; every file restored byte-identical (0 residual markers). The prompt half is asserted structurally on the file because it is the half most likely to be quietly tidied away by a later editor, and one case asserts the "Top 3 priorities" section still EXISTS: deleting it would also stop the invention, by removing the most useful part of the brief. The goal is a priority list honest about its own provenance, not no priority list. Full serial suite green: 389 files passed / 2 skipped, 4,823 passed / 50 skipped / 1 todo, exit 0. tsc --noEmit clean.  NOT CLAIMED: no brief was generated against a live LLM and no Telegram message was sent as part of this verification. The prompt rule is asserted to be PRESENT and correctly worded; whether a given model obeys it on a given morning is not something a unit test can establish, and the structural half — the block never being empty — is what makes the failure legible even if the model ignores the instruction. NOTE ON THIS KEY: last-writer-wins by design; the manifest lives on main while requirements are derived per-diff.

capability-ledger-updated.deferred: No capability gains or loses a state, so no ledger entry is edited. The rule fires on one changed file under server/services/**: opportunityQueue.ts. That change is one additive field on topDecisions' return — `queryable: boolean`, false when the queue could not be CONSULTED at all (no database handle, or revenue_opportunities missing because migration 0099 is unapplied). Both of those cases already returned an empty result and still do; the field only lets a caller tell them apart from 'asked, and there is genuinely nothing to do'. No query changed, no ranking changed, no row is written, no new surface is exposed, and the populated path is byte-for-byte identical — a test asserts the listed block still renders decisions verbatim with value, evidence and attempts, and still prints 'value unknown' rather than $0. Nothing nickstire CAN DO changed. The operator-facing change is that the morning brief now admits when the priority queue was unreadable instead of letting the model invent priorities — a truthfulness fix to an existing output, not a capability. Checked rather than assumed: there is NO ledger entry for the revenue-opportunity queue or for the morning brief. The nearest by name is `shadow-planner` (Shadow-mode opportunity planner, integration_verified), and it is not the right home — it describes the planner that PROPOSES opportunities, not the read path that surfaces them in the brief, and its state is unaffected by an additive boolean on a consumer-side query. This PR also deliberately does not CREATE an entry for the queue. Registering a capability is a claim about what the system does, and the honest state for revenue_opportunities depends on whether migration 0099 is applied in production — which this change neither applies nor verifies. Minting an entry on the strength of a unit-tested boolean is exactly the unearned claim this ledger exists to prevent. EVIDENCE for the behaviour change lives on the operator-walkthrough entry: server/ros083BriefPriorities.test.ts (9), mutation-verified three ways, plus server/__tests__/bridge-shapes.test.ts staying green to show the additive field did not drift the bridge contract.
